items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: And my cousin, the mother of this friend of mine, we called her Congetta

ctx.x: Yes. That’s right. Okay. Good example: When I was in Indiana University in 1965 to 1967 I was always — well my friend Medgar Evers had been killed and President Kennedy had been killed, and I was in a recording session and my dear friend Dr. Martin

Luther King was killed. I was in a recording session. And Dr. King — and when I was in Jackson, I was eating lunch with Medgar Evers, Dr. King was eating lunch next door in a place called the College Inn, and he had a lot of celebrities like Harry Belafonte, Lena Horne, Sammy Davis Junior, James Baldwin, I saw all of those people in Jackson, when they came through Jackson. And I remember one time there was six of them all there in this place College Inn, and those people that I named, Harry Belafonte, you know,…
That kind of empathy and character it seems has stayed with you. Do you believe it’s found its way into your composing and your visual artwork?
